newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign buying drives Bombay shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying drives Bombay shares higher.

text.p: A flurry of foreign institutional demand bucking weak first quarter company results drove Bombay shares higher on Thursday, brokers said.
"There's an abundance of liquidity," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "Foreign funds are accumulating quality stocks."
He said they were undeterred by poor first quarter results as fund managers expect a strong revival in the second half of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).
The 30-share BSE index rose 61.34 points, or 1.45 percent, to a provisional 4,306.23.
Another trader said Japanese funds were among the buyers.
Shares of tobacco firm ITC Ltd led the surge, rallying 42.75 rupees to 515 on the BSE.
"ITC is leading the rally today," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Lloyds Securities. "The first quarter reports are having an effect on the price."
The Business Standard newspaper on Thursday quoted unnamed sources as saying that ITC's net profit was up 34 percent in the first quarter ended June 30.
ITC officials were not available for comment.

TISCO closed 1.25 rupees lower at 218.50. After trading closed for the day, TISCO Chairman Ratan Tata told a shareholders' meeting that first quarter sales were lower by 10 percent against the same period a year ago.
Castrol rose 8.0 rupees to 688. It has risen about 60 percent in the last two months on expectations of a bonus issue. Company officials declined comment.
Rasesh Maniar, a dealer at brokerage Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd, said the absence of sellers was pushing the market higher.
"Even small investors have stopped selling," he said. "People are looking for opportunities to buy."
